plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the concentration mandate and reduce overall exposure.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
This significantly reduces your true leverage and potential margin call risk.
Focus on income (QQQI) and broad index (SPY, QQQ) for stability.
Maintain a large cash buffer by selling these positions.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdown. Expect reduced upside potential compared to other modes.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Reduce all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to small positions (1% or 0.5%) to reduce overall leverage.
Buy VRT at 4% as a new position, based on its strong scanner read.
This plan balances broad index and quality tech with a small amount of leverage.
The total adds are balanced by the trims and cash generated.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality setup. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Buy VRT at 6%, ERX at 5%, and XLE at 5% to lean into high-scoring scanner setups.
Add to SOXL and METU, increasing their positions to 6% each, utilizing leveraged ETFs.
This plan concentrates in strong setups and uses leverage to stretch growth.
Maintain strict stop discipline given the increased risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of higher potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs; strict stop discipline is critical.

income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth, rotating into income-focused ETFs. Remember that distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
